NPWS fees: Watagans and Tomaree National Parks do not appear on https://www.nationalparks.nsw.gov.au/passes-and-fees/fee-collecting-parks (Bouddi and Brisbane Water, in the other half, do: $8 per day listed for the list's standard entries).

entries.name: Fort Scratchley

facts.claim: Built on the Newcastle East headland in 1882 to defend against a possible Russian attack and now a museum; its guns were first fired in anger on 8 June 1942 during the Japanese submarine shelling of Newcastle; the Army left in 1972.
Open Wednesday to Monday 10:00am to 4:00pm, last entry 3:30pm, closed Tuesday.

Self-guided visits cover the Parade and Ceremony Grounds, galleries and collections but not the tunnels. Guided tunnel tours run at 10:30, 11:30, 1:10, 1:40 and 2:30 on open days; allow 90 minutes on site; tunnel tour adult $16.50, concession $11, child (4-14) $9.50, family $42, under 4 free.
Wikivoyage: Wed-Mon 10AM-4PM, refurbished and open to the public, with views to the north and over the city.

The council site fortscratchley.nsw.gov.au is the function-centre/venue-hire site and its opening-hours page redirects to the Society site.
entries.bio_suggestion: An 1882 harbour fort and museum with guided tunnel tours, shelled by a Japanese submarine in 1942.
unverified: Public-holiday closures (a council snippet lists Good Friday, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year's Day; page not loaded).

entries.name: Watagans National Park

facts.claim: NPWS: rainforest park an hour from Newcastle with walking, biking, lookouts and campgrounds; Gap Creek Falls walk; Monkey Face and Gap Creek lookouts; Boarding House Dam picnic area; more than 40 Aboriginal sites.
Roads are unsealed; only some are 2WD-accessible in dry conditions, most need 4WD; there is no public transport.
Current alerts (reviewed October 2026): Gap Creek Forest Walk part-closed for rockfall risk; Heaton Road access closed by landslip; aerial baiting notice.
Watagans is not on NPWS's list of fee-collecting national parks (no vehicle entry fee); camping is separate.

entries.name: Richmond Vale Railway Museum

entries.name: Stockton Beach

facts.claim: Stockton Beach runs about 32 km from Newcastle's Stockton breakwall north-east to Anna Bay in Port Stephens, with dunes over 30 m high.
NPWS: the largest moving coastal sand dune in the southern hemisphere lies at Worimi Conservation Lands beside Tomaree National Park; Birubi Point Aboriginal Place gives Worimi context.
Worimi Conservation Lands: entry is free for walkers, bike riders and horse riders; driving on the beach and dunes needs a beach vehicle permit (4WD only): 3-day $33, annual $88.

Wikivoyage: most easily visited on a guided tour (4WD, camel, sand-boarding from Birubi); you can stroll around the visitor centre at Birubi Beach for free; Sand Dune Safaris runs daily 9:30AM-4:30PM, $40 single.

entries.cost_note: Free on foot; $33 3-day vehicle permit for 4WD; guided dune tours roughly $40+ (Wikivoyage, June 2024).
entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: Worimi Conservation Lands (joint-managed park); loaded, HTTP 200, title "HOME - Worimi Conservation Lands".
entries.bio_suggestion: A 32 km beach with huge moving sand dunes, reached from Birubi Point for 4WD, camel and sandboarding tours.
unverified: Beach-vehicle permit prices were read from the 2026-era Worimi page; tour prices are Wikivoyage's, mid-2024.

entries.name: Mount Tomaree

Tomaree National Park is not on the fee-collecting list (no entry fee).

entries.name: Tomaree National Park
